title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
layout_note: A short linear lead-in (SfM points -> Initialization -> 3D Gaussians) feeds a loop: 3D Gaussians -> Projection -> Differentiable Tile Rasterizer -> Image, with Adaptive Density Control below Projection closing the cycle back to the Gaussians. A Camera box enters Projection from above.
grouping: No containers or tints. The forward/backward split is made by arrow colour alone: black arrows for the operation flow, light-blue arrows running the other way beside them for the gradient flow, keyed in a boxed two-entry legend at the bottom right.
shapes_depth: Flat square-cornered rectangles: processing steps filled light grey with thin dark outlines, data endpoints (Camera, Image) left white. The two data ends are drawn as data, not boxes: the SfM input is a scatter of black dots and the central '3D Gaussians' node is a cluster of soft green blurred ellipses with a bold label under it. Arrows are curved black/blue pairs around the loop and straight between boxes.
proposed_highlight: The representation itself is the visual centre: the only coloured, non-box node is the blurred green ellipse cluster, labelled in bold, sitting where every loop arrow begins and ends. The rasterizer and density control are ordinary grey boxes.
lesson: Make the scene representation the hub of the optimisation loop and draw it as its own primitives (soft coloured ellipses), with paired black forward and light-blue gradient arrows so the differentiable path reads without words.
notes: venue from the PDF: 'ACM Trans. Graph. 42, 4' (SIGGRAPH 2023 journal paper; venue_source: pdf). Caption is cropped at the right edge in the crop but the drawing is complete. Measured with the crop's two zero-height images_px boxes dropped (they cover no pixels but make `kb measure` raise 'y1 must be greater than or equal to y0'); the result equals what a fixed measure would give.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: an optimisation loop drawn as a ring around the 3D Gaussians: Gaussians -> Projection (top) -> Differentiable Tile Rasterizer (right) -> Adaptive Density Control (bottom) -> back into the Gaussians, with curved arrows closing the cycle

relations.form: a straight left-to-right lead-in on the middle row: SfM point scatter -> Initialization box -> 3D Gaussians cluster
curved paired arrows run Gaussians -> Projection -> Rasterizer and Rasterizer -> Adaptive Density Control -> Gaussians, forming one loop to the right of the Gaussians
a Camera box above-left of Projection sends a single straight arrow into it, the view entering the loop from the side
the rendered Image box at far right is linked to the Rasterizer by a black forward arrow and a blue gradient arrow back, the rendered-vs-image comparison implied, not drawn as a loss

channels.colour: line colour = direction of flow (black operation flow, light-blue gradient flow, keyed in a boxed legend); green fill appears only on the 3D Gaussians, marking the representation
channels.shape: grey-filled rectangles = operations, white rectangles = data endpoints (Camera, Image); the SfM points and the Gaussians are drawn as their own primitives (dots, blurred ellipses)
channels.line: solid arrows throughout; colour, not style, separates forward and backward passes
channels.frame: no grouping frames; only the legend is boxed

quality.strengths: the representation is drawn as data (blurred green ellipses, black dot scatter) and is the only saturated element, sitting at the hub where the loop starts and ends; forward/gradient arrows are paired side by side so differentiability reads without words; the loop geometry itself shows the optimisation
quality.weaknesses: the training target (ground-truth image vs render, the loss) is not drawn - the Image box only has arrows to the rasterizer, so what is compared stays implicit; the blue arrow from the Rasterizer to Adaptive Density Control mixes a gradient signal into the loop without saying what it carries

insights.structure: A short left-to-right lead-in (SfM point scatter -> Initialization -> 3D Gaussians) feeds a loop in which Projection (top) and Adaptive Density Control (bottom) sit between the Gaussians and the Differentiable Tile Rasterizer, which then pairs with an Image box at far right.
insights.data: The two data ends are drawn as data rather than boxes: SfM points as a scatter of black dots and the 3D Gaussians as a cluster of soft blurred green ellipses; Camera and Image are white boxes, processing steps are grey boxes.
insights.emphasis: The only coloured, non-rectangular element is the green Gaussian cluster with a bold label, placed at the hub where every loop arrow starts and ends.
insights.flow: Black curved arrows carry the forward operation flow clockwise around the loop while light-blue arrows run beside them in the opposite direction for gradients, keyed in a two-entry legend at the bottom right.
insights.avoid: The Camera box enters only Projection with a long straight arrow and floats unaligned above the loop; the rasterizer-to-Image arrows are a cramped pair.

arrangement.units: unenclosed flat grey/white rectangles plus two free-floating data glyphs (dot scatter, Gaussian cluster); no containers
arrangement.inputs_as: scatter of black SfM points; Camera box enters from the top
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; gradient flow shown by blue reverse arrows
arrangement.shared: the 3D Gaussians hub is shared by projection and density control branches
